seo.satHubH1: Explore Live Radio on an Interactive Satellite Globe
seo.satHubIntro: Spin a photorealistic 3D satellite globe and discover thousands of live radio stations from around the world, plotted by their real broadcast location — free, no signup required.
seo.homeCategoriesIntro: Live TV channels are organized into 25+ categories — News, Sports, Movies, Music, Kids, Documentary, and more — so you can browse by what you want to watch instead of scrolling through everything.
seo.homeRadioIntro: Thousands of free live radio stations, organized by genre — Pop, Jazz, Talk, News, Oldies, and more. Browse the {link1} or switch to the Radio tab above the globe.
seo.homeWebcamsIntro: Live camera feeds from cities, landmarks, beaches, and nature spots worldwide — free, no signup. Browse the {link1} or switch to the Webcam tab above the globe.
seo.homeLanguagesIntro: Every channel is also organized by language — 84+ in total — so you can find something to watch in the language you actually speak, not just the country you're browsing.
seo.homeCountriesIntro: Every one of the 200+ countries FreeTV Garden covers has its own dedicated page of channels — pick yours below, or browse by continent from the full list.
seo.homeInstallIntro: FreeTV Garden isn't on the Play Store or App Store — it installs straight from your browser instead, on any device, in a few taps.
seo.homeInstallAndroid: Open Chrome (or another browser that supports web installs) and go to freetvgarden.com. Look for the install icon in the address bar, or open the browser menu and choose "Add to Home Screen" / "Install App." FreeTV Garden will then open full-screen from your home screen, just like a native app, with no download from the Play Store required.
seo.homeInstallIOS: Open freetvgarden.com in Safari. Tap the Share icon, then "Add to Home Screen." This adds an app icon to your iPhone or iPad that launches the site full-screen — no App Store listing needed, and nothing to keep updated.
seo.homeInstallSmartTV: Open your TV's built-in browser and navigate to freetvgarden.com. If your TV doesn't have a usable browser, cast the page from your phone or laptop using Chromecast or AirPlay to watch on the big screen instead.
seo.homeInstallFire: Open the Silk Browser (pre-installed on Fire TV devices, or free from the Amazon Appstore) and go to freetvgarden.com. Select a country or category and start watching — no subscription or additional app required.
seo.homeInstallDesktop: Any modern desktop browser works — just visit freetvgarden.com. In Chrome or Edge, an install icon appears in the address bar to add it as a desktop app; otherwise it runs fine as a regular browser tab.
seo.homeFaq1A: Yes. There's no signup, no subscription, and no payment at any point — just pick a country or channel and start watching.
seo.homeFaq2Q: Is tv.garden the same as FreeTV Garden?
seo.homeFaq2A: No. The original tv.garden rebranded to Famelack in 2026 and no longer uses the TV Garden name. FreeTV Garden is a separate, independently run site — not affiliated with Famelack or the original tv.garden.
seo.homeFaq3Q: Does FreeTV Garden have the same features as TV Garden?
seo.homeFaq3A: Yes, plus more. FreeTV Garden has the same spin-the-globe, pick-a-country experience, along with 84+ language filters, 25+ content categories, picture-in-picture playback, favorites you can star and revisit, a random-channel button, and one-tap install straight from Chrome or Safari — no app store needed.
seo.homeFaq4Q: Does FreeTV Garden also have radio and webcams?
seo.homeFaq4A: Yes. FreeTV Garden also has a Radio tab with live stations across genres like Pop, Jazz, and Talk, and a Webcam tab with live camera feeds from around the world. Switch tabs above the globe.
seo.homeFaq5Q: How is FreeTV Garden different from radio.garden?
seo.homeFaq5A: FreeTV Garden is a separate, independently run project — not affiliated with radio.garden. It offers a simpler, more intuitive interface with easier navigation, and goes beyond radio with live TV and webcams built into the same free, one-tap tool.
seo.homeFaq6Q: What happened to the old FreeTool TV Garden page on Odoo?
seo.homeFaq6A: It relaunched here. The page that used to live at freetool.odoo.com/tv-garden is the same project, now running under its own name and domain: FreeTV Garden.
seo.homeFaq7Q: Do I need to create an account?
seo.homeFaq7A: No account is needed. FreeTV Garden doesn't ask for an email, password, or any personal details to watch.
seo.homeFaq8A: Yes — FreeTV Garden runs in any modern mobile browser on Android or iPhone, and can be added to your home screen for one-tap access (see the Install section above).
seo.homeFaq9A: Channels are live streams sourced from public broadcasters, so some go offline temporarily due to the broadcaster's own server issues. Try another channel, or check back later — most come back within a few minutes to hours.
seo.homeFaq10Q: Are the streams legal to watch?
seo.homeFaq10A: FreeTV Garden aggregates publicly available live streams — primarily from the iptv-org community directory — and doesn't host or store any video files itself. See the Legal & Safety section below for more.
seo.homeFaqMore: More questions are answered on the full {link1}.
seo.homeLegal: FreeTV Garden aggregates publicly available live streams from free, public sources, including the iptv-org community directory. It doesn't host or store any video or audio files, and doesn't require an account to use.
